name: Curaçao
summary_text: Curaçao: autonomous country within the Kingdom; penal code modernised; Willemstad has the Caribbean's oldest organised community; conservative interior. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: Netherlands (0.79) plus a local delta of -0.06. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Safety and travel information - Pride Amsterdam 2027
sources.claim_summary: WorldPride Amsterdam 2026 safety and travel page (about the Netherlands, included here because Curaçao is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands): border/airport procedures, Schengen passport rules, and a dedicated transgender and non-binary visitor section.

sources.title: Netherlands | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for the Netherlands (updated March 2026): progressive laws with gaps - legal gender change requires a medical expert letter; 'X' marker only via a 3-9 month court procedure; the Transgender Act (self-ID) was withdrawn in July 2025. Curaçao follows Dutch Kingdom law with its own local framework.

sources.title: Aruba - Gay and LGBT Friendly Caribbean Travel Destination
sources.claim_summary: Aruba's official tourism LGBT vacations page (Kingdom context for Curaçao): markets the Dutch Caribbean as welcoming to all visitors.

sources.title: Aruba Votes for LGBT Civil Union as first Island in the Caribbean
sources.claim_summary: Aruba tourism site news: Aruba voted for LGBT civil unions as the first Caribbean island - Kingdom-wide context for Curaçao's own recognition of same-sex marriage (2018 court ruling).

sources.title: Gay Life in a Tolerant Society in Aruba - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz report (2017): 'Gay Life in a Tolerant Society in Aruba' - describes the ABC islands (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao) as quiet nests of gay-friendliness within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, tolerant and mostly open.

sources.title: 'Snel homorechten in alle delen van het Koninkrijk' - Caribisch Netwerk
sources.claim_summary: Caribisch Netwerk (April 2015, in Dutch): 'Quickly gay rights in all parts of the Kingdom' - representatives of all Kingdom governments agreed LGBT people on Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten should quickly get equal rights; a wishes package was presented in The Hague; documents Curaçao's Gay Pride permit difficulties (2013) and the Curaçaoan government's stated support despite parliamentary opposition.
